dimensions.name: Accreditation & Quality Assurance
dimensions.summary: No regional body accredits primary/secondary schools; efforts focus on higher education through the SADC Qualifications Framework (SADCQF) and UNESCO/HAQAA workshops.
dimensions.improvementScope: Extend SADCQF-style quality assurance mechanisms down to school-level STEM provision, using UNESCO/HAQAA workshops as a model for building shared standards.
actions: Map existing national school QA bodies and identify common ground for a light-touch regional STEM accreditation standard
Pilot a voluntary regional accreditation mark for STEM programmes/schools that meet agreed minimum criteria
Extend HAQAA-style peer-review workshops from higher education down to secondary STEM provision

dimensions.name: Standardised Curriculum Frameworks
dimensions.summary: Each country maintains its own national curriculum (reviewed roughly every 5 years). Systems are structurally similar (12-13 years of schooling, English as medium of instruction in senior secondary) but content, depth and pedagogy diverge.
dimensions.improvementScope: Develop a SADC STEM Competency Framework defining minimum learning outcomes for primary and secondary STEM, linked to the SADCQF but applied to school-level exit competencies, enabling comparability without mandating a single curriculum.
actions: Draft a SADC STEM Competency Framework specifying minimum exit-level learning outcomes for maths and science
Map each member state's national curriculum against the framework to identify gaps and overlaps
Link the framework formally to the SADCQF as a school-level companion instrument

dimensions.name: Externally Benchmarked Assessments
dimensions.summary: No SADC-wide school-leaving exam exists. Individual countries use national examination boards. Cambridge/IB are used in private international schools but are not the regional standard.
dimensions.improvementScope: Introduce a voluntary regional STEM benchmark assessment (sampling-based, akin to TIMSS/SACMEQ) that allows systems to compare proficiency without replacing national exams.
actions: Adopt or expand a sampling-based regional STEM assessment (e.g. aligned to SACMEQ/TIMSS methodology) across all member states
Publish comparable regional STEM proficiency benchmarks on a recurring cycle
Use benchmark results to inform national curriculum review cycles

dimensions.name: Teacher Quality & Mobility
dimensions.summary: SADC Teacher Standards and Competencies exist, but application to STEM-specific teacher training is uneven. Few TVET instructors combine subject knowledge, industrial experience and pedagogical skill.
dimensions.improvementScope: Establish regional STEM teacher certification standards and promote exchange programmes, extending the SADC Protocol's principle of treating students as local in member states to STEM teachers.
actions: Define a regional STEM teacher certification standard built on the existing SADC Teacher Standards and Competencies
Launch a STEM teacher exchange/secondment programme across member states
Require industrial-experience components for TVET STEM instructor certification

dimensions.name: Gender Equity in STEM
dimensions.summary: Girls' proficiency in maths and science at the end of schooling lags boys' across the region, and women are underrepresented in STEM higher education and leadership.
dimensions.improvementScope: Standardise gender-disaggregated data collection on STEM participation and achievement, and coordinate regional campaigns and targeted financial support as recommended by UNESCO.
actions: Mandate gender-disaggregated STEM participation/achievement reporting across all member states
Coordinate a regional girls-in-STEM campaign with shared messaging and materials
Pool and target scholarship/financial support for girls and women in STEM

dimensions.name: Regional Collaboration & Centres of Excellence
dimensions.summary: Successful bilateral models exist (e.g. South Africa-Eswatini science roadshows, South Africa-Mozambique higher education/TVET agreement). The SADC University of Transformation concept is in development.
dimensions.improvementScope: Scale existing bilateral partnerships into a network of SADC STEM Centres of Excellence for secondary education, piloting standardised enrichment programmes, teacher training modules and shared lab resources.
actions: Formalise a network of SADC STEM Centres of Excellence building on existing bilateral partnerships
Pilot shared/virtual laboratory resource-sharing across at least 3 member states
Standardise STEM enrichment and teacher-training modules for use across the network

dimensions.name: Qualification Recognition for Mobility
dimensions.summary: Current recognition systems are often symbolic and fail to address structural labour-market barriers. Only a few SADC states have ratified key global conventions.
dimensions.improvementScope: Prioritise operationalising the SADCQF for STEM qualifications specifically, requiring technical alignment plus political will to streamline verification and build mutual trust in QA mechanisms.
actions: Prioritise STEM qualifications in the operational rollout of the SADCQF
Streamline cross-border verification processes for STEM qualifications
Encourage ratification of relevant global recognition conventions by remaining member states
